rounds.text: Viceroy Hotels Ltd is demonstrating powerful compounding fundamentals, highlighted by a 33% compounded sales growth over 5 years and a 24% expansion in sales over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. Operational efficiency is scaling rapidly, with the operating margin reaching 28% in the TTM compared to just 13% three years earlier, alongside a quarterly operating margin of 26% in June 2026 that outpaced the year-ago quarter by 11 percentage points [E27, E28]. Profitability has proven exceptional over medium-term horizons, registering a 22% profit CAGR over 5 years and a remarkable 617% compounded profit growth over 3 years [E19, E20]. Cash generation remains robust, backed by a cash conversion ratio of 3.22x and operating cash flow of Rs 58 Cr for March 2026, which proves that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash [E31, E32]. Market momentum completely supports this fundamental strength, as the share price trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a strong relative-strength rating of 83 against the Nifty 500 [E46, E47]. Conceded: [E21, E33, E36, E41].

Viceroy Hotels Ltd carries an aggressive valuation that is unsupported by its underlying financial returns, trading at an elevated P/E of 48.9x compared to a sector benchmark of 24.87x [E1, E6]. This rich pricing coincides with a low return on equity of 6.87% matching the sector benchmark and a subdued ROCE of 5.55% that trails the sector's 8.18% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 122 per share against a market price of ₹ 145, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -18.8% [E2, E41, E42]. The company's recent expansion drive has caused borrowings to surge to Rs 264 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 52 Cr previously, generating a heavy negative free cash flow of Rs -65 Cr [E33, E36]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a five-year profit growth CAGR of 22.4% [E17, E56]. Finally, insider dilution is evident as promoter holding has dropped by 20.97 percentage points to 74.03% as of September 2026, alongside heightened annualised volatility of 63.9% [E38, E50].

Conceded: the P/E ratio stands at 48.9x and the discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at ₹ 122 against the market price of ₹ 145 [E1, E2, E41]. However, evaluating this business strictly on static valuation ignores a dramatic operational turnaround where results score 95 out of 100 with net profit surging 148% year-over-year [E67]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 264 Cr and free cash flow reached Rs -65 Cr [E33, E36], but this reflects an aggressive growth phase where capital work-in-progress jumped 280% to Rs 57 Cr and operating cash flow hit Rs 58 Cr with full cash backing of 3.22x [E31, E32, E37]. Furthermore, the bear's focus on historical returns misses the multi-year trajectory of operating margins expanding by 15 percentage points in the TTM to 28% alongside a 33% five-year compounded sales growth rate [E15, E27]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased by 20.97 percentage points to 74.03% [E38], yet the stock maintains strong relative strength at 83 and trades comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E46, E47].

Conceded: net profit surged 148% year-over-year and results score 95 out of 100 [E67]. However, this is heavily offset by a trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth of -69% and a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 1% [E14, E21]. Conceded: operating cash flow hit Rs 58 Cr with a 3.22x conversion [E31, E32], but free cash flow simultaneously plunged to Rs -65 Cr alongside a massive surge in borrowings from Rs 52 Cr to Rs 264 Cr [E33, E36]. Conceded: 5-year compounded sales growth is 33% and operating margins expanded by 15 percentage points [E15, E27], yet today's market price already demands an aggressive 20.4% earnings growth assumption, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -18.8% based on intrinsic value [E41, E42, E43]. Conceded: the stock trades above its moving averages with a relative strength of 83 [E46, E47], but this momentum coincides with an extreme annualised volatility of 63.9%, a negligible Sharpe ratio of 0.05, and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.7% [E49, E50, E51]. Finally, the bull's dismissal of insider movement ignores a sharp dilution in promoter backing, with holdings dropping by 20.97 percentage points down to 74.03% [E38].
